A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DiffSoup research work, with complete, readable main text and supplementary Sections A–F. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction-quality, rendering-speed, ablation, and resource-use results in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and triangle-budget experiments.

M1.justification: The stochastic opacity masking, visibility gradients, multi-resolution textures, deferred-shading MLP, and optimization procedures are identical. The parameter-count corrections do not introduce an architectural or algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same novel-view synthesis tasks on MipNeRF360, NeRF-Synthetic, and Shelly, with identical scene and test-scenario coverage throughout the appendices.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: 3DGS, Triangle Splatting, and TexGS in the main real-scene comparisons; MobileNeRF and its QEM-decimated variant in synthetic comparisons; and 3DGS-MCMC in supplementary Tables A3–A4.

E3.justification: Primitive budgets, texture and MLP configurations, training schedules, metrics, and testing resolutions are unchanged. Table 3 revises aggregate parameter counts; the unchanged configurations and Appendix B.6 support interpreting these as accounting corrections, not revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: The opacity, multi-resolution, and coarse-to-fine ablations remain identical, as do the BICYCLE failure-case analysis and triangle-budget studies in Figures A4–A5 and Tables A2 and A6.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including scene-level averages. Neither version provides additional repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 increases every reported parameter count tenfold: 3DGS and Triangle Splatting each change from 88.5K to 885K, TexGS from 15.1M to 151M, and both DiffSoup rows from 6.75M to 67.5M. This is a localized numerical correction; FPS, reconstruction scores, memory/storage results, rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations are unchanged, including Appendix C's derivations of selection probabilities, the likelihood-ratio gradient identity, and the opacity score term.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about extreme primitive reduction, direct differentiable opaque rasterization, reconstruction quality, and cross-platform rendering.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including difficulties with transparency, thin structures, and large outdoor scenes. The parameter-count correction preserves relative ratios, including the stated approximately 170-fold TexGS-to-3DGS ratio.

D1.justification: Implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, texture specifications, MLP architecture, training times, and code-access information are unchanged. Appendices A–B and the supplementary resource disclosures contain no revisions.

R1.justification: The same 62 references and related-work discussion appear in both versions, with unchanged positioning against differentiable rasterization, NeRF, and Gaussian-splatting approaches.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 28 March 2026 to v2 dated 15 August 2026. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions, and content placement are unchanged. Table 3 changes only numerical entries, without redesigning the display.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects a tenfold understatement of parameter counts in Table 3, improving consistency with Appendix B.6's per-primitive texture sizes and Table A5's memory figures. This improves reporting accuracy without changing the method, performance evidence, or comparative conclusions.
